A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GM/TGM research, despite the changed title and DCG-to-DCP terminology. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original sampling and training results on TF-Bind-8, bit sequences, UTR, AMP, and GFP, including hyperparameter analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original results on these tasks and adds an extended GFN temperature sweep and measured training throughputs in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The GM operator, trajectory constraint, network architecture, and VarGrad procedure remain substantially the same. However, the displayed loss changes from subtracting r(x) in v1 Section 5 to subtracting beta*r(x) in v2 Section 4.2, while both experimental appendices define r(x)=beta*Phi(x). The PDFs do not resolve whether this is an intended objective change or inconsistent notation.

E1.justification: Both versions use TF-Bind-8, 120-bit sequence generation, UTR, AMP, and GFP with the same represented data and sequence requirements. The additional temperature and runtime experiments retain this coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds validation-set maximum rewards as explicit reference comparators in Table 2 and Figure 2. The evaluated algorithmic comparators remain GFN, SAC, and PPO, alongside the same TGM interpolation variants.

E3.justification: v2 Table 2 reports maxima reached during training, explicitly specified in Appendix F.4.1, replacing v1's biological learning curves and final-evaluation emphasis. Appendix B.1 adds GFN beta settings from 512 through 8192. Equation 1 also changes the stated candidate score from a sum of Phi to an average of exp(Phi), without clearly explaining whether experimental scoring changed accordingly.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.1 tests whether much larger GFN reward exponents can account for TGM's advantage, extending the sensitivity analysis beyond beta=256. Appendix B.2 adds measured computational-efficiency comparisons. The earlier interpolation, hyperparameter-robustness, and multistep-uncertainty analyses remain.

E5.justification: The principal biological comparisons explicitly increase from five seeds with standard-deviation shading in v1 Figure 5 to fifteen seeds with standard errors in v2 Table 2. This changes both replication and the uncertainty quantity reported across all three biological tasks.

E6.justification: v2 replaces biological learning curves with fifteen-seed maximum-over-training results, including GFP scores of 1.90±0.03 for GFN and 2.95±0.08 for TGM q=0.25; these are not direct same-setting improvements over v1. It adds validation maxima, throughput measurements, and extended-beta findings, while removing the TF-Bind-8 GFN beta=16 density result.

T1.justification: v2 introduces formal accumulation/dilution definitions, operator bounds in Table 1, and new propositions and proofs in Appendix C. Equation 1 changes the candidate-set objective, and the motivating example adds an explicit positive reward lower bound. The new accumulation proof incorrectly asserts positive partial derivatives, although Equation 15 gives negative derivatives near zero.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain an interpolated GM operator, trajectory-based TGM training, a compositional robustness interpretation, and improved generation of diverse high-reward candidates. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion primarily reorder and reframe these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds accumulation versus dilution as a mechanism explanation and interprets the extended-beta results as evidence that TGM explores different distributions. It removes v1's substantive limitations concerning proxy generalization and proxy-informed uncertainty sets, as well as the broader-impact appendix. A tree-structure restriction remains stated in Section 4.

D1.justification: Appendix F.1 newly specifies PPO gamma=1; v1 did not state its value, so this establishes disclosure rather than a setting change. Appendix B adds precise sweep settings, per-task training speeds, and the additional log-softmax cost explanation. Architecture details, hardware specifications, and the code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: The same 56 cited works are retained. Related work moves from Section 6 to Section 2, and the detailed comparison with prior robustness-regularization research moves into Appendix A.5, preserving the substantive positioning.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the abstract and introductory narrative, changes the title and DCG terminology, moves related work forward, and presents operator development before the robust-RL interpretation. Main-text explanations are condensed or transferred into captions and appendices.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the biological learning-curve figure with Table 2 and adds the bounds table, temperature-sweep figure, and throughput table. The earlier robustness boxplots become Figure 5, Figure 1's panels are reordered, and Figure 2 gains validation-reference markers. The document also adopts a different typographic template.

improvement.justification: The fifteen-seed estimates, extended GFN sweep, and runtime table strengthen empirical documentation. However, v2 removes learning curves and substantive limitations, compares final GFN sweep scores with TGM maxima over training, and introduces unresolved reward-scaling notation. Its new theoretical support also contains an incorrect derivative-sign argument in Appendix C. These benefits and unresolved validity and transparency problems prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
